status.en: 408 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 17% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces seized a Kuki-Zo insurgent camp in Manipur, arrested a KNF (MC) cadre and a Kuki militant, and recovered foreign-made firearms, grenades and ammunition, while the Manipur chief minister linked the violence to a pervasive gun culture and urged surrender of illegal arms. The CRPF director general and Assam Rifles chief reviewed Manipur security and held high-level meetings on law and order, calling for peace and joint operations. In Jammu and Kashmir, the lieutenant governor chaired unified command meetings and the IGP called for action against over-ground workers and hybrid terrorists, with arrests for leaking security information to foreign handlers. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker beslagla en Kuki-Zo-opprørsleir i Manipur, arresterte en KNF‑(MC)‑medlem og en Kuki-militant, og gjenvant utenlandske skytevåpen, granater og ammunisjon, mens Manipur-statsministeren knyttet volden til en gjennomgripende våpenkultur og oppfordret til overgivelse av illegale våpen. CRPF-direktøren general og lederen for Assam Rifles gjennomgikk sikkerhetssituasjonen i Manipur og holdt høytstående møter om lov og orden, med oppfordring til fred og felles operasjoner. I Jammu og Kashmir ledet lederen for unionsterritoriet felles kommandomøter, og IGP oppfordret til handling mot over-grunnsarbeidere og hybride terrorister, med pågripelser for lekkasje av sikkerhetsinformasjon til utenlandske håndterere. UCDP registrerte 437 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
